item.title: Version 3.95
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.95

Type [[ and pick a note

  • Start a wikilink and cyberWriter offers the notes to finish it - in the Markdown editor and in WYSIWYG alike. Recent notes first, then filtering as you type.
  • Matches titles, then frontmatter aliases, then folder paths. Pick a note found by its alias and you get [[Note|Alias]], so the link resolves while reading the way you searched for it.
  • [[#tag lists every note carrying that tag - partial tags work, and a second word narrows inside it (#project spec).
  • Each row tells you why it matched. Arrow keys to move, Return or Tab to insert, Escape to keep the brackets you typed. One Undo takes the whole link back.

Image captions and figures

  • An image on its own line becomes a figure, with its alt text as the caption: ![Cross-section of the hull](hull.png). Vault embeds caption with a pipe: ![[hull.png|Cross-section]].
  • Optional figure numbering (Settings or the PDF export options) prefixes captions with "Figure 1." in document order, renumbering as you reorder. Pin one by writing it - ![Figure 7. Hull](hull.png) stays 7 and the sequence continues from 8.
  • Embeds can be sized: ![[shot.png|300]] or |300x200.
  • Figures never split across a page in PDF export.

Bring your own CSS

  • A custom stylesheet applied to every note's preview and to PDF and HTML export - heading colours per level, line length, margins, paragraph spacing, whatever you want to write.
  • It's a real file you can edit in any editor, keep in version control, or sync between Macs. Edits appear on the next render.
  • Loads after the theme, so your rules win. A starter template shows which selectors to reach for.

GLOW terminal

  • demo - a guided tour that runs real commands against your vault, at your pace.
  • dump - save the session's transcript to a note.
  • A live greeting on every open: your vault, its counts, your model, the note you're in.
  • The AI on the prompt line now remembers the conversation, takes dragged-in files as context, and works with Apple Intelligence.

Faster, and more finished

  • Tooltips everywhere. Every button in every panel explains itself on hover - reliably, which the old ones did not.
  • Faster saves on large vaults. Saving no longer does work proportional to the whole vault.
  • Faster sidebar. Opening the file browser with the graph expanded no longer waits for the graph to draw.
  • The AI Workspace opens with somewhere to start instead of a wall of instructions, and offers to index your vault once rather than assuming.
  • Markdown images written as ![](shot.png) now resolve anywhere in your vault, the same way ![[shot.png]] always has.
  • Clearer license activation errors when a server reply can't be read.

Also recent (3.9): the GLOW terminal itself - a command line for your vault with your AI model on the prompt line; the PLATO appearance, rose icon and rose graph shape; LaTeX \(…\) and \[…\] delimiters in the editor.

item.title: Version 3.9
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.9

GLOW — a terminal for your vault

  • A built-in command line in a phosphor drawer over your vault. Familiar commands — ls, cd, cat, grep, find, tree, wc — plus vault-native ones: links, backlinks, tags, recent, stats, and this (the note you’re in)
  • Your AI model on the prompt line. Pipe any command into it (grep TODO | ai "summarize these"), send the answer straight into a note (… > this), and let it read, search, and edit files — with run for its built-in scripts and undo to take any change back
  • Dock it, pull it down as a shade, or pop it out into its own window

PLATO — a new face

  • A new PLATO appearance joins the roster (alongside Cyber, Blackout, and System Light/Dark) — a warm phosphor finish across the whole app
  • A refreshed rose app icon and launch splash
  • The knowledge graph takes on the rose shape

Editing & AI

  • LaTeX written with \(…\) and \[…\] now typesets in the editor — math pasted from an AI reply or the web just renders
  • AI replies that arrive wrapped in a stray ```markdown fence now format correctly instead of showing as raw code
  • The ⌘/ insert menu fans Mermaid and Vega out to every chart type through fly-out submenus
  • The typed Properties chip strip comes to the Mac editor

Fixes & polish

  • PDF export hardened against an off-main-thread WebKit measurement
  • Vault Analyze tools are cancellable with live progress, and sync-conflict false alarms are fixed
  • The serializer no longer escapes a literal $ to \$
  • Complete open-font licenses and in-app acknowledgements
  • WYSIWYG scroll-lock, scroll-inheritance, and ghost-dirty-document fixes

Also in 3.8, if you’re catching up

  • The rich-text view (⌘4) graduated to a full WYSIWYG editing surface
  • Live Data api blocks and Dataview-style query blocks, with API keys in the Keychain
  • Vega & Vega-Lite charts, Excalidraw drawings, and a Vault Map atlas
  • A typed Properties panel, Unlinked Mentions, and a Vault Health Report

item.title: Version 3.8
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.8

WYSIWYG editing, for real

  • The rich-text view (⌘4) graduates from beta to a full editing surface — write in formatted text with live tables, charts, math, and diagrams
  • AI streaming, dictation, find & replace, the ⌘/ insert menu, Properties, and live data blocks all work natively inside it
  • Flip between source and WYSIWYG anytime — your Markdown stays clean, byte for byte

Live Data blocks

  • Drop an api block into any note, click Run, and the response renders as a formatted table — baked into the document so it exports everywhere
  • query blocks filter your vault’s frontmatter into live Dataview-style tables
  • API keys live in the macOS Keychain as {{secret}} references — never in your files — and every run lands in a browsable API History

Vega & Vega-Lite charts

  • Publication-grade charts from a fenced block — live in the preview, themed to your appearance, exported to PDF, Word, and HTML
  • Twelve quick-inserts plus a gallery document; bind chart data to .json / .csv files in your vault and the chart follows the file

Excalidraw drawings

  • A full whiteboard canvas — offline and private. .excalidraw files are first-class documents
  • Embed drawings in notes with ![[drawing.excalidraw]] — they render in preview and every export
  • The new Vault Map draws your entire vault’s link graph as a clickable Excalidraw atlas

Properties & query blocks

  • Frontmatter grew up: a typed Properties panel edits tags, dates, and fields inline — no YAML wrangling
  • Obsidian-style comma-separated tags are recognized, and edits write back clean list syntax

Build a wiki from plain notes

  • Unlinked Mentions finds every place a note’s title appears without a link and connects it in one click, right from the sidebar
  • The new Vault Health Report rounds up broken links, orphan notes, and duplicate titles

Tables, paste & folding

  • Paste from Excel, Numbers, the web, Word, or Mail and it lands as clean Markdown — tables included
  • Tab through table cells, add and delete rows or columns, convert text to tables, format on the fly
  • A floating selection toolbar puts formatting at your cursor; any block folds away with ⌘. when you need the room

Faster with huge vaults

  • Multi-thousand-file vaults scroll, search, and index smoothly — AI indexing moved fully off the main thread with a subtle status-bar indicator instead of popups
  • Saves rescan only what changed; drag-and-drop stays responsive during background work

More

  • The interactive Feature Guide is now Help (⌘?) — searchable cards for every feature
  • KaTeX color sugar: $...$:color tints any equation, plus a Math insert menu
  • Native macOS Version History from the toolbar and vault menu
  • New Apropos theme with bundled Nunito Sans & Noto Sans; theme fonts now flow into WYSIWYG
  • Theme-aware Mermaid diagrams with per-chart [bg:COLOR] cards
  • Vault: Show All Files toggle, Open As (Plain Text / Hex), folder context menus, Restore Example Vault
  • Smarter first-launch flow, wikilink hover cards that render KaTeX and Mermaid, dozens of editor-hardening fixes

Also recent (since 3.6)

  • A full appearance system — System Light, System Dark, and pure-black Blackout alongside the original Cyber identity
  • Knowledge Graph reimagined — tag-colored nodes, a guided tour, and search that lights up matching notes
  • Snippets manager — capture, organize, pin, and embed reusable text (⌘⌥S shade)
  • Voice upgraded — input-device picker, live waveform, and words streaming in as you speak

item.title: Version 3.7
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.7

Welcome screen fixes

  • Fixed the preview occasionally getting stuck on a “Loading Preview…” placeholder for an empty document — the welcome screen (recent files & quick start) now appears right away, no reload needed
  • The welcome screen now follows your App Appearance: pure black in Blackout, true light in System Light, and dark in System Dark — it no longer borrows the editor’s document theme

Also recent (since 3.6)

  • A full appearance system — System Light, System Dark, and pure-black Blackout alongside the original Cyber identity
  • Knowledge Graph reimagined — tag-colored nodes, a guided tour, and search that lights up matching notes
  • Snippets manager — capture, organize, pin, and embed reusable text (⌘⌥S shade)
  • Voice upgraded — input-device picker, live waveform, and words streaming in as you speak
  • Faster large-document rendering, instant theme switching, and smoother tab switching

item.title: Version 3.6
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.6

A real light mode — and Blackout

  • A full appearance system, tuned end to end: System Light and System Dark now read crisply everywhere — accents, borders, panels, and the knowledge graph all retuned for contrast
  • New pure-black Blackout mode for OLED-style depth, alongside the original Cyber identity. Pick your look in the toolbar or Settings → Themes

Knowledge Graph, reimagined

  • Your vault as a living globe — tag-colored nodes cluster by topic, and a guided tour walks the graph for you
  • Search lights up matching notes (brighter and larger means more relevant); float it in its own window or keep it inline in the sidebar

Snippets

  • A built-in snippet manager — capture reusable text from any document, organize it in folders, and pin favorites
  • Drop a snippet anywhere from the snippets shade (⌘⌥S), or embed and link snippets right inside your notes

Voice, upgraded

  • Pick your input device, watch a live waveform while you talk, and see words stream into the editor as you speak
  • Dictation and AI insertions anchor cleanly at the cursor without disturbing the text around them

Faster everywhere

  • Large documents open and render dramatically faster, switching themes is instant, and moving between tabs is smoother
  • The knowledge graph pauses when the app is in the background, so cyberWriter sips power instead of gulping it

Launch polish

  • A refined first-launch animation, and the trial / license prompt now waits politely behind it

item.title: Version 3.0
item.description:
cyberWriter 3.0

WYSIWYG editor (beta)

  • A new visual editing surface where formatting renders inline instead of as markdown syntax — write the way the doc reads
  • Hit ⌘4 to enter it (no toolbar button — this is an early beta, opt-in only)
  • All of cyberWriter's custom syntax round-trips through it: wikilinks, vault embeds (10 file types), Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, callouts, page breaks, hex color swatches, tags
  • Same AI Quick Actions (⌘J), voice transcription, and slash-command palette work in the visual surface
  • Themes apply live — Cyber, System Light, System Dark, and the document theme picker all drive WYSIWYG typography and color
  • ⌘F find with next/prev (⌘G / ⌘⇧G), pinch-to-zoom, body font size +/-, PDF preview round-trip
  • Marked clearly with an orange BETA pill while it's still being polished — Crepe's hide-markdown-once-formatted behavior and a few HTML embed quirks are known and on the punch list

item.title: Version 2.97
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.97

App Appearance

  • New three-way picker in Settings → Themes: Cyber (the original Synthetic Editorial dark identity), System Light, or System Dark
  • Cyber preserves the exact original look pixel-for-pixel — nothing changes if you've been here all along
  • System Light and System Dark hand window chrome to macOS so cyberWriter blends with the rest of your apps; the editor and preview keep their own document themes independent of this setting
  • Light mode polish throughout — pale-blue toolbar tint, dark brand-text variants for legibility on white, mode-aware sidebar accents, light-friendly knowledge-graph background

License management

  • New Settings → License tab: status badge, masked key, and one-click Change License Key / Deactivate actions
  • Deactivate now releases this Mac's activation slot on the Lemon Squeezy server, so you can move your license to another machine without contacting support
  • License key field auto-trims whitespace on paste — messy email pastes with stray spaces or newlines just work

Editor & AI

  • AI chat now renders Markdown HTML reliably — no more occasional raw-tag passthrough
  • Vault search results jump to the matching line on click instead of just opening the file
  • Tag pills colored by hash by default — categories scan faster across many notes (toggle in Settings if you prefer neutral chips)
  • Line numbers off by default for a cleaner first-launch experience (toggle in Settings)

Also recent (since 2.96)

  • Vault Stats Dashboard — one-click vault overview from the Files-tab toolbar; counts, top tags, most-linked files, orphans, recent modifications, all rendered as navigable wikilinks
  • Restored File menu items that disappeared on macOS 26 — Quick Export PDF, Export, Save to Vault, Restore Example Vault
  • Stopped runaway CPU when the About window was open or recently closed

item.title: Version 2.96
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.96

Vault Stats Dashboard

  • One-click vault overview from the Files-tab toolbar (📊 chart icon) — writes Vault Stats.md at the vault root and opens it instantly
  • Sections: file & word counts, top tags, most-linked files, orphans (files with no inbound wikilinks), recently modified, folder + file-type breakdowns
  • Every file reference renders as a [[wikilink]], so the dashboard doubles as a navigable Map of Content
  • Click the icon again to regenerate with a fresh timestamp; the existing dashboard closes and reopens with current data
  • Also accessible from the new top-level Vault menu in the menu bar, alongside Save to Vault and Restore Example Vault

Fixes

  • Restored File menu items that disappeared on macOS 26 — Quick Export PDF, Export, Save to Vault, and Restore Example Vault. Apple's expanded auto-injected document-menu group was eating the slot SwiftUI's older anchor used; commands now live on stable anchors and the new top-level Vault menu
  • Fixed runaway CPU triggered by opening the About window. Animated subviews were burning ~190% CPU and continued running even after dismissal because the timeline kept ticking and per-frame allocations grew without bound. CPU now plateaus below 30% while open and drops to baseline immediately on close

Also recent (since 2.9)

  • Multi-language input fixes — dropped accents on Spanish (and other dead-key) layouts no longer drop, and Japanese / Chinese / Korean conversions during fast typing land at the right cursor position instead of the wrong line
  • Vault embeddings: eliminated the "Indexing 0 of 1 files" flashing loop that affected some Mac configurations, especially with frontmatter-only or all-code-fence notes
  • Vault embedding progress now shows chunk-level detail with a sidebar indicator — large log files no longer beachball during indexing
  • AI chat input no longer steals keyboard focus from the ⌘/ command palette or freshly opened documents

item.title: Version 2.95
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.95

Multi-language input support

  • Fixed dropped accents and stray newlines when typing fast on Spanish (and other dead-key) layouts — the editor now defers internal updates while the IME has marked text, so compositions resolve cleanly
  • Fixed Japanese / Chinese / Korean text getting inserted on the wrong line when typing fast and converting with Space — the marked range can no longer be invalidated mid-composition
  • Same hardening applies to every IME-using language: dead keys and character conversion now land where you expect, regardless of typing speed

Vault embeddings

  • Fixed "Indexing 0 of 1 files" flashing loop on configurations where one vault file produced no embeddable chunks (frontmatter-only notes, all-code-fence notes, unreadable encodings)
  • Two-phase build (read+chunk, then embed) means progress now reflects chunk-level work — a 4000-chunk log file shows real movement instead of a silent beachball
  • New indexing pill in the vault Files-tab toolbar surfaces progress when a vault is opened from the sidebar (the top-of-window banner is easy to miss with sidebar focus)

AI panel focus

  • ⌘/ command palette now reliably claims keyboard focus from the AI chat input — typing lands in the search field, not the chat
  • New documents (⌘N, ⌘T, ⌘O) start with the cursor in the editor instead of the AI chat input

Polish

  • About: thanks to /u/Stubborninmate for excellent testing and feedback

item.title: Version 2.9
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.9

Native PDF Viewer

  • Open .pdf files in a dedicated read-only viewer window — no more bouncing out to Preview
  • Triggered from Finder (double-click), the vault sidebar, or by dropping a PDF on the app chrome
  • PDFs dropped directly into the editor still embed as before — the editor's drop handler wins on its own area
  • Powered by PDFKit's PDFView: continuous-scroll, autoscale, page breaks, search, and thumbnail navigation come for free
  • Each PDF gets its own window, independent of any Markdown editor — close the editor without losing your reference docs

Configurable Line Spacing

  • New "Preview & Export Typography" setting in Preferences → Export controls line height for the live preview and PDF / Word / HTML exports
  • Discrete presets: Theme default, 1.0, 1.15, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0, 2.5 — matches Word/Pages, no slider ambiguity
  • Per-document override via YAML frontmatter — drops in front of the global setting:
---
title: My Doc
line-height: 1.7
---
  • Editor pane intentionally untouched — keeps tracking the system default for fastest typing feel

AI Chat: Continuity Across Windows

  • New Document (⌘N), New Tab (⌘T), and Open... (⌘O) now carry your active AI conversation into the new window
  • Previously only vault wikilink clicks did this — now the menu paths match
  • Both windows stay synced via the shared conversation manager — type in either, see it in both

Reliability

  • Vault embeddings: eliminated the first-launch flashing loop when Apple Intelligence is off, still downloading, or warming up — the indexing banner now appears once and only when there's real work to do
  • Embedding builds persist progress every 25 files instead of 100, so an interrupted build resumes from where it left off
  • Sparkle auto-updates fire predictably the moment you accept the permission prompt — no more waiting until tomorrow for the first check
  • Sparkle check interval lowered from 24h to 1h so updates land within an hour of release
  • Update checks now flow from GitHub Pages going forward — same EdDSA signature key, no action required, future releases land automatically

Polish

  • Knowledge Graph: thinner edge widths so dense graphs read less crowded, especially at low zoom
  • AI Quick Actions: "POPULAR" badge restyled in normal case for visual consistency with surrounding chrome

item.title: Version 2.8
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.8

Chat with Your Vault

  • On-device semantic embeddings via Apple's NLContextualEmbedding — your notes, indexed locally, never sent anywhere
  • AI answers grounded in your own vault: ask a question and the top matching chunks are spliced into context automatically
  • Per-conversation toggle in the AI panel and a global switch in AI Settings
  • Optional vault structure summary so the AI knows every file that exists, even ones it didn't directly retrieve
  • Works with every provider — Apple Intelligence, Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio
  • Vault Map report — see exactly what was embedded, when, and why files were skipped

Concept Search

  • Vault search bar now surfaces a "Related Ideas" section beneath exact matches
  • Search "spaceship" and find notes about orbits, rockets, and trajectories — even when the word never appears
  • Auto-updates as you edit files, with a Build / Rebuild / Clear panel in AI Settings

Rendered AI Responses

  • AI chat now renders markdown — headings, lists, code blocks, bold/italic
  • Vault filenames in responses become clickable wikilinks that open the file
  • Toggle back to plain text in the AI panel header if you prefer the raw view

Feature Tour

  • Interactive spotlight tour walks new users through every toolbar feature
  • Available from the welcome screen and the Help menu, anytime
  • First-launch users land in a populated UI with vault and AI panel open

Polish

  • New documents (Cmd+N, +Tab, templates) reliably inherit the source window's sidebar layout
  • Apple Intelligence: clear status detection on macOS 26+ with a one-click deep link to System Settings if it's installed but disabled
  • Knowledge Graph node labels render above their dots — readable at every zoom
  • Voice transcription stays in the active document instead of duplicating across every open window
  • Vault embeddings respect vault switches — no stale chunks leaking between vaults

item.title: Version 2.6
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.6

Performance

  • 6x faster preview rendering on large documents
  • DOM diffing (morphdom) — only changed content re-renders
  • Cached syntax highlighter eliminates repeated initialization

Polish

  • CSV/TSV files render as interactive tables in preview
  • Non-editable vault files open with system default handler
  • File extensions shown for non-text files in vault sidebar
  • Vault highlight matches by file path, not just name
  • Escape key no longer exits native fullscreen
  • Styled AI quick actions text input

item.title: Version 2.5
item.description:
cyberWriter 2.5

  • Flash Cards with SM-2 spaced repetition
  • Presentation mode: zoom, mermaid/KaTeX, title slides
  • Apple Intelligence (on-device AI, macOS 26+)
  • No more keychain password prompt on launch
  • Auto-updater fixed
